p6_b4.ocr: For instance, the results reveal a compelling correlation between the type of cannula used and the mean chondrocyte viability percentages, highlighting the importance of mechanical factors in cellular outcomes. In the case of the "Large bore" cannula, a striking mean chondrocyte viability of 93% was recorded, underscoring its potential advantages in maintaining cell integrity during procedures.

p6_b5.ocr: Furthermore, the degree of fibrosis was assessed across varying conditions, providing a comprehensive understanding of tissue response in the presence of different binding types. Collectively, these metrics serve to inform best practices in biomedical applications involving chondrocytes and set the stage for future research aimed at optimizing conditions for cellular preservation and minimizing fibrotic development. The implications of these findings are crucial for advancing strategies in tissue engineering and regenerative medicine.
